ai_tweets.headline: Nano Labs launches ClawPC A1 Mini — dedicated hardware for OpenClaw agents
ai_tweets.detail: Nano Labs (Nasdaq: NA) officially announced the iPollo ClawPC A1 Mini, purpose-built hardware for running OpenClaw agents. This is the first publicly traded company shipping dedicated AI agent hardware. Listed on Business Insider's markets section.
ai_tweets.takeaway: A Nasdaq-listed company is now shipping hardware specifically for OpenClaw. Combined with the $5 MimiClaw from Hackster.io, the hardware layer for AI agents is materializing fast. The ecosystem is no longer software-only.

ai_tweets.headline: Google officially opens Workspace to OpenClaw and AI agents via new CLI
ai_tweets.detail: Google released a Workspace CLI that explicitly supports OpenClaw integration. Covered by Mashable, The Next Web, and Technobezz. Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and Contacts now have first-class agent access with MCP integration built in.
ai_tweets.takeaway: Google naming OpenClaw in their official docs is a legitimacy milestone. The gog skill we already use just got an official blessing. Expect more enterprise integrations to follow Google's lead.

ai_tweets.headline: PleaseFix: Critical vulnerabilities found in agentic browsers including Perplexity Comet
ai_tweets.detail: Zenity Labs disclosed PleaseFix, a family of critical vulnerabilities affecting agentic browsers. Attackers can hijack agent browsing sessions and exfiltrate data. Covered by Help Net Security.
ai_tweets.takeaway: The attack surface for AI agents keeps expanding. Last week it was CVE-2026-25253 (OpenClaw auth tokens), this week it's agentic browsers. If your agent browses the web, review what permissions it has and what data it can access.

ai_tweets.headline: Coruna iOS exploit kit now weaponized for crypto theft
ai_tweets.detail: A spyware-grade iOS exploit kit called Coruna is being used in active crypto theft attacks. BleepingComputer reports it targets wallet apps and can exfiltrate seed phrases from compromised devices.
ai_tweets.takeaway: If you hold crypto on iOS (which most of us do), this is a real threat. Update iOS immediately and audit which apps have accessibility/notification permissions. Hardware wallets looking smarter by the day.

ai_tweets.headline: GPT-5.4 leak: 1M context window, 'Extreme Reasoning Mode', monthly update cadence
ai_tweets.detail: AI Leaks and News reports upcoming GPT-5.4 will feature 1M context window, a new extreme reasoning mode, improved memory, and better long-horizon task performance. OpenAI reportedly shifting to monthly model updates.
ai_tweets.takeaway: If real, 1M context changes the game for long-running agent sessions — no more compaction anxiety. Monthly updates mean the model you optimize for today might shift next month. Stay flexible with model routing.

prompt_hack.title: The 'Plan-Execute-Verify' Loop — Kill the Dropout Pattern
steps: From r/openclaw's top post this week (104 upvotes): agents that chain 10+ tool calls without self-checking gradually lose coherence — the 'dropout pattern'.

Add this to AGENTS.md: 'Every 5 tool calls, pause and verify: (1) Am I still on track with the original request? (2) Did my last actions produce the expected results? (3) What's my next step and why?'

For complex tasks, enforce explicit structure: '## Plan
[write plan before starting]
## Execute
[do the work]
## Verify
[check results match plan]'
The key insight: agents don't fail suddenly — they drift. Forcing periodic self-checks catches drift before it becomes a hallucination spiral.
Bonus: add 'If you notice you're repeating actions or getting unexpected results, STOP and reassess before continuing.' to your AGENTS.md.
prompt_hack.why_it_matters: The dropout pattern post was the most-discussed topic on r/openclaw this week. Multiple users confirmed a ~60% reduction in agent errors just by adding periodic self-check prompts. Zero cost, immediate improvement.

model_radar.detail: The entire Qwen3.5 lineup is sweeping HuggingFace trending: 9B (692K downloads), 35B-A3B (1.08M downloads), 27B (630K), 4B (282K), 0.8B (346K). All are multimodal (image-text-to-text). The unsloth GGUF versions are equally hot with 1M+ downloads for the 35B-A3B variant alone.

model_radar.relevance: Video generation going local is a milestone. Not directly agent-relevant today, but content creation agents (like what we'd build for OSM clips) could eventually use local video models instead of expensive API calls.

model_radar.model: AReaL v1.0 — PyTorch-native RL for Agent Evolution
model_radar.detail: Ant Ling released AReaL v1.0, a stable reinforcement learning framework specifically designed to evolve AI agents. Features a PyTorch-native 5D-Parallel engine and claims compatibility with OpenClaw-style agent architectures.
model_radar.relevance: RL-trained agents are the next evolution beyond prompt engineering. If agent behavior could be reinforcement-learned rather than prompt-instructed, the ceiling for agent capability goes way up. Early but worth watching.
